long_biography.plain_text:
Katz brought an engineering mind to Rockport. After studying engineering physics at Cornell, he applied athletic-shoe materials and lightweight orthotics to traditional leather footwear. The resulting RocSport and ProWalker lines helped define the walking-shoe category, while Rockport funded research, clubs, books and public campaigns that promoted fitness walking as accessible exercise.

After leaving the company, Katz shifted part of his attention to early online services and consumer ventures. His Rosewood Stone investment group backed web businesses including Match.com, Evite and eGreetings, and he helped create The Republic of Tea. He also used the Katz Family Foundation to support environmental, educational and social organisations, extending his entrepreneurial interests beyond footwear.
